cards.front: Where are restrictions and endorsements shown on an Indiana credential, and where are they explained?
cards.back: Restrictions and endorsements appear in the lower left corner of an Indiana credential, and their meanings are printed on the back of the card.

cards.front: What is the most common source of restrictions on permits and licenses?
cards.back: Vision screening results are the most common source of restrictions on learner's permits and driver's licenses.

cards.front: What does restriction B require of a driver?
cards.back: Restriction B means the driver must wear glasses or contact lenses when driving.

cards.front: What does restriction F require of the vehicle?
cards.back: Restriction F means the vehicle must have outside mirrors or a rearview camera whenever the holder drives.

cards.front: What does restriction G allow?
cards.back: Restriction G limits the holder to driving in daylight only.

cards.front: Who decides whether a driver with a disability gets a restricted license?
cards.back: BMV examiners decide whether a person whose disability affects normal operation of a standard vehicle gets a restricted license, which may require specific equipment or other accommodations.

cards.front: What can a restricted license for a driver with disabilities name?
cards.back: A restricted license for a driver with disabilities can name the particular equipment the driver must use in the vehicle.

cards.front: On a base license, what do endorsements L and two mean, and what does endorsement B mean on an ID card?
cards.back: On a base driver's license, endorsement L stands for motorcycle and endorsement two for for-hire, while on an ID card endorsement B stands for motor driven cycle.
cards.memory_hook: L ride, two hire, B cycle

cards.front: What do base license restriction codes C, D, J, six and eight stand for?
cards.back: Base license restriction codes include C for a mechanical aid or adaptive device, D for a prosthetic aid, J for specific limitations, six for an interlock device and eight for a medical condition.

cards.front: Which restriction codes appear on both base licenses and ID cards?
cards.back: Codes three (photo exempt), seven (seat belt exempt) and nine (lawful temporary resident) appear as restrictions on both base licenses and ID cards.

cards.front: What do restrictions H, S, two and five mean?
cards.back: Restriction H limits motorcycle riding to a three-wheel bike, S to a motorcycle with a sidecar, two marks an HTV conditional license and five means the holder may drive only under specific conditions.

cards.front: What does the letter B mean as a license restriction versus an ID card endorsement?
cards.back: On the code chart, B as a license restriction means glasses or contact lenses, while B as an ID card endorsement means motor driven cycle.

cards.front: How does restriction G differ from restriction J?
cards.back: Restriction G means daylight driving only, while restriction J on the license chart means specific limitations.

cards.front: What does the number two mean as an endorsement versus a restriction?
cards.back: Endorsement two on a base license means for-hire, while restriction two means HTV conditional.

cards.front: What do you need to get a motorcycle learner's permit?
cards.back: A motorcycle learner's permit requires a valid Indiana driver's license and a passed knowledge exam based on the Motorcycle Operator's Manual.

cards.front: What limits apply to a motorcycle permit holder?
cards.back: A motorcycle permit holder must wear a helmet, may not carry passengers, and may ride only in the daylight window that the manual bounds by one-half hour before sunrise and one-half hour after sunset.

cards.front: How long is a motorcycle learner's permit valid, and how often can it be issued?
cards.back: A motorcycle learner's permit is valid for one year and can be issued or renewed no more than three times in a five-year period.

cards.front: What happens if a rider does not earn the endorsement before the renewed motorcycle permit expires?
cards.back: If the endorsement is not earned before the renewed motorcycle permit expires, the rider must wait one year for a new permit or complete a Ride Safe Indiana safety course.

cards.front: When can a first-time license applicant receive a motorcycle endorsement with the new license?
cards.back: A first-time license applicant aged sixteen or older who has completed a motorcycle safety course can receive the motorcycle endorsement together with the new license.

cards.front: What are the two ways to earn a motorcycle endorsement at any age?
cards.back: A motorcycle endorsement requires, at any age, either a completed Ride Safe Indiana safety course or passing both the motorcycle knowledge exam and the riding skills exam.

cards.front: Which motorcycle safety courses does the BMV strongly encourage?
cards.back: The BMV strongly encourages motorcycle safety courses from Ride Safe Indiana providers, listed at RideSafeIndiana.com.

cards.front: What must a new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle endorsement do to add the Indiana endorsement?
cards.back: A new resident holding a valid motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle license from another state adds the Indiana endorsement after passing only the motorcycle knowledge exam.

cards.front: Does a new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle credential take a riding skills exam?
cards.back: A new resident with an out-of-state motorcycle credential takes the motorcycle knowledge exam only, with no riding skills exam.

cards.front: How long does a motorcycle endorsement last, and what does it cost at renewal?
cards.back: A motorcycle endorsement lasts as long as the driver's license, the license can be renewed with it up to two years early at a branch or online, and an unexpired endorsement carries no extra fee at renewal.

cards.front: How early can a license with a motorcycle endorsement be renewed?
cards.back: A license with a motorcycle endorsement can be renewed up to two years early.

cards.front: What features make a vehicle an autocycle?
cards.back: An autocycle is a three-wheeled vehicle with a fully or partly enclosed seating area, a roll cage or roll hoops, a safety belt for each occupant, anti-lock brakes and steering wheel and pedal controls.

cards.front: What credential do you need to drive an autocycle?
cards.back: A valid Indiana driver's license is enough to drive an autocycle; no motorcycle permit or endorsement is needed.

cards.front: What riding rules apply to an autocycle?
cards.back: An autocycle must be driven from a seat, without carrying a package in hand, and the manual bars operating more than one autocycle in a single traffic lane.
cards.memory_hook: seated, hands free, one per lane

cards.front: Who must wear a seat belt in an autocycle, and can it be used for a skills exam?
cards.back: Everyone in an autocycle must wear a seat belt, and an autocycle cannot be used for a driver's license skills exam.

cards.front: How do the credential rules differ for an autocycle and a motor driven cycle?
cards.back: An autocycle needs only a valid driver's license, while an MDC can be ridden on an ID card that carries an MDC endorsement.

cards.front: How does the seating position differ on an autocycle and a motor driven cycle?
cards.back: Autocycle riders sit on a seat, but MDC riders must sit astride the seat with a leg on each side.

cards.front: What makes a vehicle a motor driven cycle?
cards.back: A motor driven cycle has a seat or saddle, runs on no more than three wheels, meets state and federal equipment rules, has an engine of fifty cubic centimeters or less and is registered as an MDC.

cards.front: How is an MDC endorsement added, and who does not need one?
cards.back: An MDC endorsement is added to an ID card at its next issuance after the holder passes the MDC knowledge exam, and holders of a valid permit or license need no MDC endorsement.

cards.front: How old must an MDC rider be, and what gear must younger riders wear?
cards.back: An MDC rider must be at least fifteen, and riders under eighteen must wear a helmet plus protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield.
cards.memory_hook: fifteen to ride, gear under eighteen

cards.front: Which MDC rule applies to every rider, and which applies only to riders under eighteen?
cards.back: Any MDC rider must be at least fifteen, but the helmet and eye-protection rules apply only to riders under eighteen.

cards.front: How must an MDC be ridden?
cards.back: An MDC must be ridden astride the seat with headlamps on and without carrying a package in hand.

cards.front: Where on the road must an MDC stay, and how fast may it go?
cards.back: An MDC must stay near the right edge of the road except when passing or preparing to turn left, and may go no faster than thirty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: What may an MDC never do?
cards.back: An MDC may not carry passengers and may not be ridden on an interstate highway or a sidewalk.

cards.front: What driving does a for-hire endorsement cover?
cards.back: A for-hire endorsement covers hauling property for hire in a vehicle registered at 16,000 to 26,000 pounds gross weight, or carrying passengers for hire in a vehicle designed for fewer than sixteen people including the driver.

cards.front: Does a for-hire endorsement let you drive a commercial motor vehicle, and what must a CDL holder do to drive a cab?
cards.back: A for-hire endorsement does not permit driving a commercial motor vehicle, and a CDL holder who wants to work as a limo, cab or ride share driver must pass the for-hire exam and add the endorsement.

cards.front: Who can get a for-hire endorsement, and which exams are required?
cards.back: A for-hire endorsement requires age eighteen and at least one year holding a valid Indiana license; a new applicant passes both the driver and for-hire knowledge exams, while a current unexpired license holder takes only the for-hire exam.

cards.front: How does a new resident with an out-of-state for-hire credential add the Indiana endorsement?
cards.back: A new resident aged eighteen or older who already holds a for-hire endorsement from another state on a valid license, a chauffeur or public passenger chauffeur license, or a CDL adds the Indiana for-hire endorsement after passing the for-hire knowledge exam.

cards.front: How early can a license with a for-hire endorsement be renewed?
cards.back: A license carrying a for-hire endorsement can be renewed at a branch or online up to one year before it expires.

cards.front: Is the for-hire renewal window shorter or longer than the motorcycle window?
cards.back: A license with a for-hire endorsement can be renewed only up to one year early.

cards.front: Does the BMV require a medical examination report for the for-hire endorsement?
cards.back: The BMV does not require a medical examination report for the for-hire endorsement; drivers unsure whether their vehicle needs one should contact the Indiana Department of Transportation.

cards.front: Which kinds of transport do not count as for-hire?
cards.back: Driving a medical services vehicle, or hauling property for hire in a vehicle registered under 16,000 pounds, does not count as transporting for hire.

cards.front: What is a for-hire bus?
cards.back: A for-hire bus is a bus that carries passengers for hire or is operated for compensation.

cards.front: When is moving a recreational vehicle before its first retail sale not for-hire transport?
cards.back: Moving a recreational vehicle before its first retail sale is not for-hire transport when it weighs no more than 26,000 pounds, or when the combined weight with the towing vehicle is no more than 26,000 pounds and the towed unit is no more than 10,000 pounds.

recap_hooks.text: Restrictions sit in the lower left corner and are explained on the back; vision results cause most of them.
B means corrective lenses, F means mirrors or a rearview camera, and G means daylight only.
On a license, L means motorcycle and two means for-hire; on an ID card, B means motor driven cycle.
The same letter or number can mean different things as a restriction and as an endorsement.
A motorcycle permit needs a license and the motorcycle exam, and its holder rides solo, helmeted, in daylight.
Earn the endorsement with a Ride Safe Indiana course or both motorcycle exams.
An autocycle needs only a driver's license and belts for everyone.
MDC riders are fifteen or older, keep right, carry no passengers and stay off interstates and sidewalks.
For-hire covers paid hauling and passenger work below set limits, but it is not a commercial license.
You need age eighteen and a year licensed, and a for-hire license renews only one year early.
